_readme: Curated player notes extracted from podcast/press briefings pasted into the assistant. Hand-reviewed and version-controlled: no live model runs at build time. Notes are DISPLAY-ONLY - they never feed the simulator. Every note keeps its source and, where possible, a verbatim quote, so a reader can judge it. Names that a transcript garbled are parked in `unresolved` rather than guessed at, because attaching a note to the wrong player is worse than dropping it.

players.name: Lewis Miley
players.note: At 20, part of a young Newcastle midfield pivot; the performance was seen as a marked improvement on last season.

players.name: Ollie Watkins
players.note: Absent as Villa's spine was decimated; the side lacked depth and conceded four in 30 minutes.

players.name: Vuskovic
players.note: 19-year-old Croatian international; standout in defence, contrasting with struggling high-priced signings elsewhere (surname-only in the briefing).

players.name: Yoane Wissa
players.note: A counter-attacking threat against Liverpool's very high line in the 2-2 draw.

players.name: Youri Tielemans
players.note: Listed among the absentees that left Villa's spine decimated.

players.name: Adam Wharton
players.note: Of interest to Chelsea as an Enzo Fernandez replacement, though Crystal Palace are unwilling to sell.

players.name: Alex Scott
players.note: Of interest to Chelsea as an Enzo Fernandez replacement, though Bournemouth are unwilling to sell.

players.name: Bernd Leno
players.note: Nutmegged by Cole Palmer for Chelsea's goal after being sold the dummy.

players.name: Cole Palmer
players.note: Silky and fluid in the 3-2 win at Fulham, scoring a cheeky goal; his omission from the World Cup squad is read as a wake-up call after an injury-hit campaign.
players.quote: He just looked free, fluid, so silky, so clever on the ball... the goal was brilliant. He kind of gives Leno the eyes, makes it look like he's going to pass it back into the middle and then just rolls it through his legs. It's so cheeky. It's so Cole Palmer.

players.name: Enzo Fernandez
players.note: Persistent rumours of a move to Manchester City; Chelsea want a replacement lined up before sanctioning an exit.

players.name: Ethan Pinnock
players.note: The 33-year-old is set to join Coventry City for £5m plus £1m in add-ons, on a three-year deal with an option for a fourth.

players.name: Joao Pedro
players.note: Part of a Chelsea front three with Palmer and Rogers described as one of the most exciting attacking units in the league.

players.name: Josh King
players.note: Named in connection with Fulham's first goal, cited as an example of Robert Sanchez's poor positioning.

players.name: Liam Delap
players.note: Likely to join Nottingham Forest after being distanced from Chelsea's first-team training.

players.name: Mike Penders
players.note: Named as the young Belgian keeper Chelsea could turn to in place of Robert Sanchez.

players.name: Morgan Rogers
players.note: Part of a Chelsea front three with Palmer and Joao Pedro described as one of the most exciting attacking units in the league.

players.name: Mykhailo Mudryk
players.note: Possible loan interest from Strasbourg; a move to Leeds United is considered unlikely.

players.name: Robert Sanchez
players.note: Poorly positioned for both Fulham goals; the panic he transmits unsettles the defence. Seen as the single thing keeping Chelsea to top-four rather than title contention.
players.quote: It's not just the first goal with Josh King. It's also things like just the the panic that he transmits... It just makes the defense nervy, I think. This is Sanchez's fourth season as Chelsea's number one, and it just feels like he's been an issue for all of that period.

players.name: Adam Wharton
players.note: Called a 'jewel' and close to irreplaceable for his sublime passing and tactical awareness, amid heavy transfer interest.

players.name: Emiliano Martinez
players.note: Named among the long-serving players whose high turnover is seen as a possible breaking point for Villa's European ambitions (surname only).

players.name: Ezri Konsa
players.note: Named among the long-serving players whose high turnover is seen as a possible breaking point for Villa's European ambitions (surname only).

players.name: Ismaila Sarr
players.note: Subject of intense transfer rumours as Oliver Glasner struggles to keep his squad core together.

players.name: Jean-Philippe Mateta
players.note: Subject of intense transfer rumours as Oliver Glasner struggles to keep his squad core together.

players.name: Kieran Dewsbury-Hall
players.note: Standout performer in Everton's 4-0 Carabao Cup win over Preston.

players.name: Marmush
players.note: Named as arriving at Spurs from Manchester City; spelt 'Marmush' in the briefing, so the exact player is uncertain.

players.name: Mikey Moore
players.note: Impressed in Spurs' 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton.

players.name: Nicholas Jackson
players.note: Arriving at Villa, a significant shift in the club's striking options as Ollie Watkins leaves.

players.name: Niko Gonzalez
players.note: Signed by Newcastle from Manchester City for a reported £50m despite being seen as surplus at City; name form uncertain.

players.name: Ollie Watkins
players.note: Impending departure to Saudi Arabia, attributed to 'generational wealth', as part of a scattergun Villa rebuild.

players.name: Robert Sanchez
players.note: Faces former club Brighton with Chelsea's title hopes seen as tethered to him; opponents may look to exploit the panic he transmits.
players.quote: I genuinely believe that Chelsea could challenge Arsenal for the title... but they have to change a goalkeeper.

players.name: Savio
players.note: Arrived at Spurs from Manchester City (previously Savinho) and impressed in the 5-1 Carabao Cup win over Charlton; part of a heavy bet on unproven ex-City talent.

players.name: Anthony Elanga
players.note: His goal in the 2-0 win at Tottenham was described as the crucial moment.

players.name: Bruno Fernandes
players.note: Credited in the episode title for a brilliant display in the 5-2 win over Ipswich.

players.name: Emiliano Martinez
players.note: Called 'Emmy Martinez' in the briefing: his arrival at Chelsea is cited as evidence that a high-profile goalkeeping change can shift a title race, after the Robert Sanchez problem.

players.name: Harrison Armstrong
players.note: Attempted £40m sale of the academy prospect drew fan backlash, a case study in clubs selling homegrown 'pure profit' talent to satisfy PSR.

players.name: Harry Maguire
players.note: His handball in the buildup to a United goal was ruled accidental so the goal stood, which the panel argued rewarded a mis-hit shot.
players.quote: What [the rule] has effectively done is reward Harry Maguire for doing his job badly. By shooting off target he's rewarded, and that just shouldn't be how the rule is.

players.name: Kobbie Mainoo
players.note: Future subject to speculation despite strong performances.

players.name: Marcus Rashford
players.note: Future subject to speculation despite strong performances.

players.name: Micky van de Ven
players.note: Named among Spurs players lacking preseason integration as the side went two games without a point or a goal (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Morgan Gibbs-White
players.note: Liverpool's midfield struggled to contain him in a 2-2 draw in which Forest led twice.

players.name: Nico Paz
players.note: Named as an example of the buy-back-and-sell schemes clubs use to manage their books.

players.name: Petrovic
players.note: Made heroic saves in the 1-1 draw with Everton (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Ryan Cherki
players.note: Scored his first brace, in the 4-1 win over Crystal Palace, providing a new creative spark for City.

players.name: Arnaut Danjuma
players.note: Everton have lost him, prompting interest in a Jack Grealish loan (surname only in the briefing).

players.name: Bradley Barcola
players.note: Written 'Bradley Barker' in the briefing: linked to Liverpool, called a huge talent but not the best finisher.

players.name: Bukayo Saka
players.note: Scored the only goal at Villa Park, reacting quicker than Villa's defenders, in a win described as textbook title-winning efficiency.

players.name: Eberechi Eze
players.note: Spelt 'Eza' in the briefing: provided the weighted pass for Arsenal's goal but was criticised for an instinct to drift infield and congest the structure.

players.name: Gabriel Jesus
players.note: Written 'Gabrielle Jesus' in the briefing: linked to Barcelona for a fee around £15m.

players.name: Jack Grealish
players.note: Potential loan to Everton following their loss of Danjuma.

players.name: Julian Alvarez
players.note: Wants to leave Spain and is rumoured to Arsenal, with Atletico seeking around £150m.

players.name: Lionel Messi
players.note: Announced a second retirement from international football, saying he has nothing left to give and wants to make room for younger players.
players.quote: I have loved, and will always love being part of the national team. I've given it my all. I have nothing left to give.

players.name: Lucas Digne
players.note: Among nine Villa departures this summer, six of whom started the Europa League final.

players.name: Morgan Rogers
players.note: Listed among Villa's summer departures, part of a squad overhaul that has left them without a shot on target this season.

players.name: Mykhailo Mudryk
players.note: Written 'Michaela Mudryk' in the briefing: linked to Tottenham and a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, having been training in Battersea Park.

players.name: Riccardo Calafiori
players.note: Named man of the match; his darting run created Arsenal's winner at Villa Park.

players.name: Bernd Leno
players.note: Poised to join Robert Huth, Dietmar Hamann and Pascal Gross as the only German players to reach 250 Premier League appearances.

players.name: Beto
players.note: Sold on deadline day, one of the departures that left Everton with only 18 senior players.
players.quote: I think what was shaping up to be an okay transfer window for Everton turned into an absolute shambles at the end of it.

players.name: Bruno Fernandes
players.note: The player a depleted Everton midfield has to neutralise, in the briefing's preview of Everton v Manchester United.

players.name: Enzo Fernandez
players.note: The move rumoured on 25 Aug has completed: a £125m transfer from Chelsea to Manchester City, the marquee deal of the window.

players.name: Folarin Balogun
players.note: His move to Everton collapsed at the last minute on deadline day, leaving them without a recognised striker.

players.name: Iliman Ndiaye
players.note: Sold on deadline day alongside Beto, deepening Everton's squad crisis.

players.name: Joshua Zirkzee
players.note: A failed Everton pursuit; with Abraham and Balogun also missed, Everton ended the window without a striker.

players.name: Malick Fofana
players.note: Spelt 'Malik Fofana' in the briefing. Chose Sunderland over Crystal Palace, reportedly on a larger offer from the Sunderland chairman and the presence of a second private jet — cited as an example of the grotesqueness of modern transfers.

players.name: Mykhailo Mudryk
players.note: Spelt 'Milkyo Mudrich' in the briefing. The Spurs move flagged on 1 Sep has gone through; cited as significant investment that still leaves Tottenham's 'mentality' questioned.

players.name: Phil Foden
players.note: Named among the established stars the new midfield arrivals must fit around; the briefing calls City's midfield rotation a selection headache after the Fernandez signing.

players.name: Ryan Cherki
players.note: Spelt 'Sherkey' in the briefing. Named beside Foden as an established starter whose place the new signings complicate.

players.name: Taiwo Awoniyi
players.note: Coventry's raw striker, cited as the hit-or-miss type of signing — Max Rushden reached for Gattuso to describe him.
players.quote: Sometimes maybe good, sometimes maybe s***.

players.name: Tammy Abraham
players.note: A failed Everton pursuit in a window the briefing calls a shambles.

players.name: Aaron Wan-Bissaka
players.note: Also not ready to come on against Hull City, alongside Abraham.

players.name: Ainsley Maitland-Niles
players.note: Scored a 96th-minute equaliser against Manchester United — his second career Premier League goal, and his first in eight years.

players.name: Alexander Isak
players.note: Two goals at Ipswich; touted as the premier striker in the league after Haaland.

players.name: Cody Gakpo
players.note: Two assists at Ipswich, continuing a strong start after a frustrating previous season.

players.name: Declan Rice
players.note: Named as the closest thing the Premier League has to a genuinely game-defining central midfielder, in a discussion about clubs overpaying for versatile all-rounders.

players.name: Diogo Dalot
players.note: His deployment was criticised as part of the tactical indecision that cost United the game at Everton.

players.name: Dominic Solanke
players.note: Injured, part of the forward shortage behind Spurs' goalless start.

players.name: Erling Haaland
players.note: Used as the benchmark the briefing measures other Premier League strikers against.

players.name: Federico Valverde
players.note: Cited alongside Bellingham as the calibre of midfielder the Premier League is paying for but not getting.

players.name: Florian Wirtz
players.note: Struggling with the Premier League's tempo, appearing to rush his play rather than dictate it as he did in Germany.

players.name: Gianluigi Donnarumma
players.note: A near-error against Coventry City, reflecting an inconsistent performance despite several saves.
players.quote: I thought he had the first touch of a street mugger.

players.name: James Maddison
players.note: Injured, part of the creative shortage behind Spurs' goalless start.

players.name: Jude Bellingham
players.note: Cited as an example of era-defining midfield genius that the Premier League currently lacks.

players.name: Kai Havertz
players.note: Produced the game's decisive moment in the 2-1 win over Chelsea: a choreographed dummy that left Odegaard the winning goal.
players.quote: This was probably the moment of grace that I think the game deserved... a moment of genius.

players.name: Marcus Rashford
players.note: Impactful before being substituted in the 2-2 draw at Everton; taking him off was criticised as unsettling the team.

players.name: Martin Ødegaard
players.note: Scored the winner against Chelsea and is described as purring in a way injury prevented last season.

players.name: Moises Caicedo
players.note: The other half of Chelsea's injury-prone midfield base.

players.name: Omar Marmoush
players.note: Has yet to fill the void left by Spurs' departed scorers; the briefing questions whether a hybrid attacker should be carrying a traditional number 9 role. Earlier episodes spelt him 'Marmush'.

players.name: Riccardo Calafiori
players.note: Being deployed high up the pitch, cited as one of Arsenal's new tactical wrinkles.

players.name: Richarlison
players.note: A departed scorer whose goals Spurs have not replaced — they have yet to score this season.

players.name: Romeo Lavia
players.note: One half of Chelsea's primary midfield base; the briefing's standing concern is how injury-prone that pairing is. Chelsea finished the Arsenal game with two right-backs in midfield.

players.name: Son Heung-min
players.note: A departed scorer named alongside Richarlison in Spurs' goalless start.

players.name: Tammy Abraham
players.note: Not ready when Emery wanted to bring him on against Hull City, visibly frustrating the manager — cited as internal friction.

players.name: Tyrick Mitchell
players.note: Scored his second in Palace's 3-2 win at Fulham, the ball clanking off his standing leg on the way in.

players.name: Tyrique George
players.note: Scored with a single touch to set and a powerful finish from a tight angle in the 2-2 draw with Manchester United.

players.name: Alex Iwobi
players.note: Reported to have deleted social media posts after defeats, cited as a sign of dressing-room friction under Arbeloa.

players.name: Curtis Jones
players.note: Integrating well into Inter's midfield, though an underhit pass led to a goal.

players.name: Denzel Dumfries
players.note: Named as the preferred right-back, which is what pushes the Alexander-Arnold position question. The briefing places him at Inter, but he is in Real Madrid's squad here — it also quotes Mourinho as Real's manager and praises Real's keeper, so the summary appears to have swapped the sides of the tie.

players.name: Emile Smith-Rowe
players.note: Named alongside Iwobi as a senior player deleting social media posts amid Fulham's unrest.

players.name: Erling Haaland
players.note: Scored twice in the 2-0 win at Porto, reaching 59 goals in 59 Champions League appearances. The briefing's point is how little he needs the ball to decide a game.
players.quote: Harland's ridiculous and he needs to touch the ball five times and he can score two goals for you.

players.name: Ethan Mbappé
players.note: Sent off for an elbow in Lille's 3-2 defeat at Real Betis.

players.name: Ethan Nwaneri
players.note: The injuries to Karetsas and Konstantelias have accelerated his integration; the briefing expects an extended run and rates him in both offensive and defensive phases.

players.name: Gianluigi Donnarumma
players.note: Booked again at Porto — ten yellow cards since joining City, mostly for complaining and minor infractions, described as a pattern of silliness.

players.name: Giannis Konstantelias
players.note: Suffered an ACL tear, the second of Dortmund's two serious injuries to major signings. Spelt 'Giannis Constantellas' in the briefing.

players.name: Hakan Calhanoglu
players.note: Named in Inter's controlling midfield; spelt 'Chalanoglu' in the briefing.

players.name: John McGinn
players.note: Scored what the panel called a beautiful curler in the 3-2 win at Club Brugge.

players.name: Josep Martínez
players.note: Sommer's replacement in goal: spectacular saves, but gifted Real Madrid a goal with a failed dragback in his own area. Spelt 'Yusef Martinez' in the briefing.

players.name: Jude Bellingham
players.note: Denied by Courtois among the chances in the 2-1 win over Inter. The briefing places him at Inter, but he is in Real Madrid's squad here — it also quotes Mourinho as Real's manager and praises Real's keeper, so the summary appears to have swapped the sides of the tie.

players.name: Konstantinos Karetsas
players.note: Hospitalised with respiratory issues — one of two major Dortmund signings lost to injury. Spelt 'Constantinos Caretsas' in the briefing.

players.name: Nicolas Jackson
players.note: Scored against Club Brugge after their keeper's error, in Villa's 3-2 win.

players.name: Nicolò Barella
players.note: Part of an Inter midfield the briefing says controlled the game despite the defeat.

players.name: Piotr Zielinski
players.note: Named in the Inter midfield credited with significant control against Real Madrid.

players.name: Serhou Guirassy
players.note: Scored an own goal off his face in the 3-2 win over Villarreal.

players.name: Thibaut Courtois
players.note: Several crucial saves in the 2-1 win over Inter, described as the stabilising force in the side.

players.name: Trent Alexander-Arnold
players.note: Mourinho said publicly that he is not a midfielder despite being used there for England and Liverpool, with Dumfries preferred at right-back. The briefing places him at Inter, but he is in Real Madrid's squad here — it also quotes Mourinho as Real's manager and praises Real's keeper, so the summary appears to have swapped the sides of the tie.
players.quote: Actually, Trent Alexander-Arnold played midfield with England and Liverpool, but he's not a midfielder.

players.name: Troy Parrott
players.note: Scored winners against both Real Madrid and Lille; his finishing is credited with reviving Pellegrini's Betis.

players.name: Alexis Mac Allister
players.note: Spoke publicly before the Atletico Madrid comeback about not being offered a new contract while team-mates were. The panel read it as a delicate negotiation in public rather than a request to leave, noting his emotional celebration in front of the Kop afterwards.
players.quote: There was lots of sadness. There was praise. There was emotion. Didn't say I wanted to leave.

players.name: Cole Palmer
players.note: Named as part of the firepower behind the 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds — a side scoring freely but conceding at a rate the panel thinks is unsustainable.

players.name: Florian Thauvin
players.note: Re-emerging as a veteran leader, with crucial headers in high-drama European fixtures.

players.name: Kai Havertz
players.note: Cast as the perfect forward for this Arsenal side, in a digression on why tall, skilful players are judged more harshly on aesthetics — the panel's 'Havertz Trutherism'.
players.quote: I was trying to posit the theory that tall skillful players look more beautiful than short skillful players... the grace of a Berbatov or a Havertz.

players.name: Martin Ødegaard
players.note: His return to peak form was put down to settled personal circumstances since the birth of his child — the panel's 'fatherhood factor', offered as a theory about him rather than a finding.

players.name: Morgan Rogers
players.note: Named with Palmer as Chelsea's attacking threat in the 6-3 win over Leeds.
